result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_lowest_common_ancestor()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check whether a node is a lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a DAG. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_lowest_common_ancestor()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check whether a node is a lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a DAG. title: >- [Graph.is_lowest_common_ancestor()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check whether a node is a lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a DAG. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check whether a node is a lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a DAG. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L59179-L59251){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_lowest_common_ancestor( node_1, node_2, candidate, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is lowest common ancestor](/assets/graphs/is-lowest-common-ancestor.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The diamond DAG A to B and C, which both point to D. Left: for the pair B, C (outlined), the top A (accent) is a common ancestor and none of its children is one, so is_lowest_common_ancestor returns True. Right: for the pair B, D, A is again a common ancestor, but its child B (accent) is one too, as B reaches D, so A is not lowest and the call returns False." width="100%"} A node is a lowest common ancestor of `node_1` and `node_2` when it is an ancestor of both (each node counting as its own ancestor) and none of its descendants is. Use it to verify a claimed merge base or shared category without listing all of them, for example to test whether a given commit is one of the merge bases of two branches. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The first node, as an integer ID or a string label. [node_2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The second node, as an integer ID or a string label. [candidate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to check, as an integer ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if `candidate` is a lowest common ancestor of the two nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or the graph is undirected or contains a cycle. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The two ancestor sets are found by backward search, then `candidate` must lie in both while none of its direct successors does, $O(V + E)$. This follows `is_lowest_common_ancestor` from NetworkX pull request #7988. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a diamond, the top is the lowest common ancestor of the two middle nodes, but not of a middle node and the bottom, since that middle node is an ancestor of the bottom: ::: {#bf08d8a8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) ( g.is_lowest_common_ancestor("B", "C", "A"), g.is_lowest_common_ancestor("B", "D", "A"), g.is_lowest_common_ancestor("B", "D", "B"), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, True) ``` ::: :::
